---
title: "Quarterly and annual statements (ITR & DFP)"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"
)
```

CVM publishes two financial-statement datasets with the **same eleven
tables** and the same schema, differing only in cadence:

* **ITR** — *Informações Trimestrais*. One CSV per table per year, with
  one row per `(company, quarter, account)`.
* **DFP** — *Demonstrações Financeiras Padronizadas*. One CSV per
  table per year, with one row per `(company, fiscal year, account)`.

The package's tooling is identical for both: pass `"itr"` or `"dfp"`
as `dataset`, the same `table` name, and the same arguments. Eight
tables out of eleven publish individual / consolidated variants
selected through `basis`.

```{r setup}
library(cvmdata)
```

## Reference: tables available

| Table                | What it carries                                        | `basis` required?       | Notes                                                        |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bpa`                | Asset side of the balance sheet                        | Yes (`ind` / `con` / both) | `VL_CONTA × ESCALA_MOEDA` applied (`multiply_by_scale`).  |
| `bpp`                | Liabilities + equity side                              | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `dre`                | Income statement                                       | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `dra`                | Statement of comprehensive income                      | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `dfc_md`             | Cash-flow statement, direct method                     | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `dfc_mi`             | Cash-flow statement, indirect method                   | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `dmpl`               | Statement of changes in equity                         | Yes                     | Idem; wider table (multiple equity columns).                 |
| `dva`                | Statement of value added (Brazilian-specific)          | Yes                     | Idem.                                                        |
| `composicao_capital` | Capital composition (share counts by class)            | No (leave unset)        | No `cd_cvm` column; indexed by `cnpj_cia`.                   |
| `parecer`            | Auditor opinion (free-text)                            | No                      | One row per filing, with full opinion text in `texto`.       |
| `submissao`          | Filing header — `id_doc`, `dt_receb`, `link_doc`, etc. | No                      | The dataset's index: one row per delivery, re-filings included; the current one is the last by `dt_receb`, `id_doc`. |

The eight tables that take `basis` always carry a `basis` column in
the result, whether you asked for one variant or for
`c("ind", "con")` (which stacks both).

Use `cvm_dictionary("dfp", "<table>")` to see the column-level
metadata (descriptions, domain, data type, size) for any of the
eleven tables; `cvm_codelist("dfp", "<table>", "<column>")` returns
enumerated categorical values.

## Workflow 1 — Side-by-side total assets across two issuers

Goal: compare 2024 total assets for **BCO BRASIL S.A.** (CNPJ
`00.000.000/0001-91`) and **MAGAZINE LUIZA S.A.** (CNPJ
`47.960.950/0001-21`) using the individual balance sheet
(`dfp/bpa`).

```{r workflow-1-fetch}
bpa <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = c("00.000.000/0001-91", "47.960.950/0001-21"),
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind"
)
bpa
```

The tibble carries provenance attributes and the package has already:

* multiplied `VL_CONTA` by `ESCALA_MOEDA` and dropped the scale column
  (values are in absolute reais);
* converted `DT_REFER`, `DT_FIM_EXERC` to R `Date`;
* kept only the filing delivered last per `(cnpj_cia, dt_refer)` — so
  re-filings do not produce duplicated rows. The `submissao` index is
  the exception: it lists every delivery, with its receipt date.

Total assets is the top of the asset hierarchy (`cd_conta == "1"`):

```{r workflow-1-summary}
ativo_total <- bpa[
  bpa$cd_conta == "1" & bpa$ordem_exerc == "ÚLTIMO",
  c("cnpj_cia", "denom_cia", "dt_fim_exerc", "vl_conta")
]
ativo_total
```

CVM publishes each fiscal year's CSV with two reference columns —
`ÚLTIMO` (the declared year, here 2024) and `PENÚLTIMO` (the
comparative previous year). To pick up an older comparative,
request the matching upstream year explicitly:

```{r workflow-1-history}
bpa_history <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2022:2024,
  basis = "ind"
)
ativo_history <- bpa_history[
  bpa_history$cd_conta == "1" & bpa_history$ordem_exerc == "ÚLTIMO",
  c("dt_fim_exerc", "vl_conta")
]
ativo_history[order(ativo_history$dt_fim_exerc), ]
```

The `PENÚLTIMO` column is the comparative the issuer presented a year
later, and issuers restate it. `reading` reads an exercise by its own
year and labels the two readings — the figures originally filed
(`ÚLTIMO` of that year's file) and the comparative of the following
year's file (`PENÚLTIMO` there):

```{r workflow-1-readings}
bpa_2023 <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2023,
  basis = "con",
  reading = c("original", "restated")
)
bpa_2023[
  bpa_2023$cd_conta %in% c("1", "1.02"),
  c("dt_refer", "ordem_exerc", "dt_fim_exerc", "cd_conta", "vl_conta",
    "reading")
]
```

## Workflow 2 — Capital composition and the filing header

`composicao_capital` does not carry `cd_cvm` — it indexes by
`cnpj_cia`, which is exactly what `cnpj` matches, so the call is the
same as for any other table:

```{r workflow-2-fetch}
cap <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "composicao_capital",
  cnpj = c("00.000.000/0001-91", "47.960.950/0001-21"),
  year = 2024
)
cap
```

Note: no `basis` argument — `composicao_capital` is a single
concept, not split into individual / consolidated, and passing
`basis` to it aborts.

Cross-check against the underlying submissao header, which is also
where a CVM code (`cd_cvm`) meets its CNPJ:

```{r workflow-2-header}
sub <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "submissao",
  cnpj = c("00.000.000/0001-91", "47.960.950/0001-21"),
  year = 2024
)
sub[, c("cd_cvm", "denom_cia", "dt_refer", "id_doc")]
```

ITR works the same way — replace `"dfp"` with `"itr"`. The trimester
breakdown then shows up in `dt_refer`, `dt_fim_exerc` and in the
`ds_conta` / `grupo_dfp` columns; the underlying mechanics
(`multiply_by_scale`, `keep_latest_version`, date conversion via
the dictionary) are shared. To pick quarters rather than whole
years, pass a `from`/`to` window on the reference date:

```{r workflow-2-itr}
h1 <- cvm_fetch(
  "itr", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  from = "2024-01-01", to = "2024-06-30",
  basis = "con"
)
unique(h1$dt_refer)
```

## Workflow 3 — Comparing companies: the CVM's fixed accounts

Each statement row carries `st_conta_fixa`. `"S"` marks an account of
the CVM's standard chart, the same in every company that follows the
chart. `"N"` marks an account the company opened under it. To compare
companies, keep the fixed accounts. The package adds no argument for
this, because the column is already there:

```{r workflow-3-fetch}
dre <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "dre",
  cnpj = c("33.000.167/0001-01", "47.960.950/0001-21", "60.872.504/0001-23"),
  year = 2024,
  basis = "con"
)
fixas <- dre[dre$st_conta_fixa == "S" & dre$ordem_exerc == "ÚLTIMO", ]
fixas[fixas$cd_conta == "3.01", c("denom_cia", "cd_conta", "ds_conta")]
```

The output shows the caveat. The CVM has more than one standard chart:
one for companies in general, others for banks and for insurers. Under
`3.01`, Petrobras and Magazine Luiza report the revenue from sales and
Itaú Unibanco reports the revenue from financial intermediation. The
code is fixed in all three charts, but it does not mean the same thing
in all of them. The CVM does not publish which chart a company follows.
`setor_ativ` in `cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias")` tells banks and
insurers apart.

What the fixed accounts are worth, measured on 2026-11-01 on the
mirror. The measurement covered every DFP (2010-2025) and ITR
(2011-2025) statement table, both bases and the current-exercise
column, about 21 million rows from about 1,200 companies:

* **Comparable within a chart.** A fixed account used by 20 or more
  companies carries one name for 99.2% of them on average (DFP
  consolidated 2024). Where the names differ, the minority is a bank
  or an insurer: `1.02.03` is *Imobilizado* for 450 companies and a
  class of financial assets for 17. A non-fixed code carries a median
  of 45 different names across companies. It is not a basis for
  comparison.
* **Stable within a company.** For the same company and account the
  flag changes between years in 0.3% of the pairs (DFP) and 0.4%
  (ITR). The changes cluster in a few years (2018, 2020, 2023), when
  the chart itself was revised.
* **Small.** Accounts fixed for at least 95% of the companies that
  use them number about 51-72 in the consolidated balance sheet
  assets (`bpa`), 100-130 in liabilities (`bpp`), 25-28 in the income
  statement (`dre`) and 10 in the cash flow (`dfc_mi`). Of the 467
  companies in the 2024 consolidated DFP, 448 carry every one of them.
  The 19 that do not are 15 banks, 2 insurers and 2 holding companies.
* **The top of the tree.** Every level-1 account (`1`, `2`, `3`...)
  is fixed, and 97.5% of level-2 rows are. The share falls to about
  70% from level 4 down, where companies open their own accounts.
